Liquid saturation distribution within the sheet at various points during one cylinder- pocket-cylinder cycle on the paper machine dryer section Due to alternate conduction and mass transfer in the pockets the sheet temperature becomes more uniform, at least while in the pockets, as compared to one sided drying reported earlier. Due to the mass transfer from both sides of the sheet in the open pockets, there is a more symmetric moisture distribution within the sheet with the top and bottom surfaces of the sheet drying first and the middle of the sheet being wetter. When the sheet is completely dried then moisture profile becomes more uniform throughout. The average temperature of the sheet as it goes through alternate sided conduction and evaporating cooling in the pockets exhibits a cyclic temperature profile (Figure 21), a characteristic of the paper machine drying. The peaks and valleys in the sheet temperature plot (Figure 21), show the heating up of the sheet reaching a maximum temperature during a given contact period with the cylinder and then reaching a minimum temperature due to evaporative cooling in the pockets at the end of a convection cycle. After the initial temperature increase during the warm-up period in the first dryer section, the overall average sheet temperature (average of the cycles shown) does remain approximately constant for a brief period after the initial warm up period and before beginning to increase during the fall rate period. 28 DE-EE0009395 Figure 21. Instantaneous and average sheet temperature during multi cylinder drying Similarly, the instantaneous drying rate also exhibits cyclic behavior as the sheet goes over the cylinders on either side and double-sided convection in the pocket (Figure 22). The peaks and valleys in the drying rate plot (Figure 22) are due to heating up of the sheet during contact with the heated cylinder, and evaporation and sudden release of vapor (and possibly liquid water) as the sheet exits the contact with the dryer. Similarly, the instantaneous drying rate then decreases during evaporative cooling (also decreasing the sheet temperature) reaching a minimum. Average drying rate which does not exhibit the cyclic behavior, does show a warmup rate, approximately constant rate and falling rate period. The duration of each of these periods is a function of the process parameters and operating conditions.
